bullets: Contributed to the Hardware Debloat research project presented through the DAC Young Fellows programme, building a QEMU/DECAF-based dynamic feature-management system across Windows XP, Windows 7, and Lubuntu guest images.

Worked within a team that developed four DECAF/QEMU plugins to dynamically control network, Q-device, block-device, and context-switching features, supporting attack-surface reduction, resource efficiency, and full-system benchmarking. Configured and troubleshot block-device storage connectivity and volumes across Linux guest images.

Developed a Python/GHIDRA static-analysis pipeline that reconstructed control-flow graphs across 40+ firmware binaries, handling indirect calls, computed jumps, recursion, and call over-approximation. Correlated static results with live DECAF execution traces to isolate defects across firmware and system layers, building automated verification mechanisms for systems-level code, and automated the pipeline with Python and Bash scripts.
